title: Implement pkg/testutils differential testing harness
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml (full PRD with all requirements R1-R5 and acceptance criteria)
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (components section -- understand how pkg/testutils fits as the shared verification layer)
  - go.mod (module path and Go version)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel01.0.yaml (test suite for ts -- shows how TimestampNormalizer is used in practice)

files:
  - path: pkg/testutils/difftest.go
    action: create
    note: DiffTest struct, Normalize type, RunDiffTests entry point, binary execution, comparison and reporting logic
  - path: pkg/testutils/normalize.go
    action: create
    note: TimestampNormalizer, ComposeNormalizers helper, and any shared normalization utilities
  - path: pkg/testutils/difftest_test.go
    action: create
    note: Unit tests for RunDiffTests, normalization, file-state comparison, and timeout behavior

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: >
      Define a DiffTest struct in pkg/testutils with fields: Name (string, used as subtest name),
      Args ([]string), Stdin ([]byte, nil means no stdin/immediate EOF), Env ([]string, nil means
      inherit test process environment), ExitCode (int, expected exit code), Normalize ([]NormalizeFunc
      where NormalizeFunc is func([]byte) []byte -- applied in order; nil or empty means no normalization),
      ExpectedFile (optional *FileExpectation struct with Path string and Content []byte for utilities
      whose output is a file rather than stdout), and WorkDir (string, optional working directory --
      empty means use a per-test temp directory created by the harness).
  - id: R2
    text: >
      Implement a RunDiffTests(t *testing.T, goBinary string, refBinary string, tests []DiffTest) function.
      For each DiffTest, call t.Run(test.Name, ...) to create a named subtest. Within each subtest:
      (a) create a temp directory if WorkDir is empty, (b) execute both binaries with identical args, stdin,
      env, and working directory, (c) capture stdout, stderr, and exit code from each, (d) apply the
      Normalize functions in order to both stdouts and both stderrs, (e) compare normalized stdout
      byte-for-byte, normalized stderr byte-for-byte, and exit codes exactly, (f) if ExpectedFile is
      non-nil, read the file at ExpectedFile.Path relative to the working directory after each binary
      exits and compare content byte-for-byte.
  - id: R3
    text: >
      Implement binary execution with a configurable timeout. The default timeout is 10 seconds.
      Use exec.CommandContext with context.WithTimeout. If either binary exceeds the timeout, fail the
      test with a clear message indicating which binary timed out. Capture stdout and stderr into
      separate bytes.Buffer instances. Extract the exit code from the *exec.ExitError (or 0 if err is
      nil). Do not write any output to the test process stdout or stderr during a passing test.
  - id: R4
    text: >
      On comparison failure, report all of: the DiffTest args, stdin content (truncated to 256 bytes
      if longer), reference binary stdout, Go binary stdout, reference binary stderr, Go binary stderr,
      reference exit code, and Go exit code. Use t.Errorf with a formatted message that includes all
      these fields. The message must clearly label each field (e.g., "Args:", "Ref stdout:", "Go stdout:").
  - id: R5
    text: >
      Implement a TimestampNormalizer (a NormalizeFunc) that replaces common timestamp patterns with
      the fixed string "TIMESTAMP". The patterns to match are: (a) syslog/default ts format matching
      the regex for "Mon DD HH:MM:SS" (e.g., "Feb 19 14:05:32"), (b) ISO-8601 datetime
      "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS" with optional fractional seconds and timezone, (c) elapsed time format
      "HH:MM:SS" at the start of a line (for ts -s and -i modes). Use regexp.ReplaceAll for each
      pattern. The normalizer is used by cmd/ts differential tests.
  - id: R6
    text: >
      Implement a ComposeNormalizers(fns ...NormalizeFunc) NormalizeFunc function that returns a single
      NormalizeFunc applying each function in order. This is a convenience for building normalizer
      chains.
  - id: R7
    text: >
      For file-state comparison (R2 step f): when ExpectedFile is set, after each binary executes,
      read the file at the given path. Compare the two file contents byte-for-byte. Report divergence
      in the same format as stdout divergence (showing both file contents and the path).
  - id: R8
    text: >
      Write unit tests in difftest_test.go that verify: (a) RunDiffTests passes when two identical
      binaries (use /bin/echo or a simple Go test helper binary) produce the same output, (b)
      RunDiffTests fails (using a testing helper that expects failure) when outputs differ, (c)
      TimestampNormalizer replaces "Feb 19 14:05:32" with "TIMESTAMP", (d) TimestampNormalizer
      replaces "00:00:05" at line start with "TIMESTAMP" (elapsed mode), (e) ComposeNormalizers
      applies functions in order, (f) a test with a timeout shorter than the binary runtime
      produces a timeout failure. For tests that need a binary, build a small Go program in a
      TestMain or use /bin/echo and /bin/cat which are available on all Unix systems.

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: >
      Use testing.T as the only test framework. Do not import testify or other assertion libraries.
      The project uses only the Go standard library plus golang.org/x/sys.
  - id: D2
    text: >
      The module path is github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils. Package import path will be
      github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils/pkg/testutils.
  - id: D3
    text: >
      NormalizeFunc is defined as a named type: type NormalizeFunc func([]byte) []byte. The DiffTest
      Normalize field is []NormalizeFunc (a slice, not a single function) so normalizers compose
      naturally without a separate wrapper. ComposeNormalizers is a convenience but the slice is
      the primary mechanism.
  - id: D4
    text: >
      Exit code extraction pattern: when exec.Command returns a non-nil error, type-assert to
      *exec.ExitError and call ExitCode(). When err is nil, the exit code is 0. When err is non-nil
      but not an *exec.ExitError (e.g., binary not found), fail the test with the error message.
  - id: D5
    text: >
      The FileExpectation struct enables sponge-style tests where the utility writes to a file
      instead of stdout. The harness reads the file after execution and compares. This avoids
      requiring each cmd/ test to implement its own file comparison.
  - id: D6
    text: >
      All regexp patterns for TimestampNormalizer should be compiled once at package level using
      regexp.MustCompile, not inside the function body, to avoid repeated compilation.

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: >
      pkg/testutils compiles with no errors: "go build ./pkg/testutils/..." succeeds.
  - id: AC2
    text: >
      go vet ./pkg/testutils/... produces no warnings.
  - id: AC3
    text: >
      go test ./pkg/testutils/... passes with all tests green.
  - id: AC4
    text: >
      RunDiffTests correctly passes when both binaries produce identical output (verified by test).
  - id: AC5
    text: >
      RunDiffTests correctly reports failure when outputs differ (verified by test using
      testing.T helper or by checking test output).
  - id: AC6
    text: >
      TimestampNormalizer replaces syslog-format timestamps ("Feb 19 14:05:32") with "TIMESTAMP"
      (verified by unit test).
  - id: AC7
    text: >
      TimestampNormalizer replaces elapsed-time timestamps ("00:00:05" at line start) with
      "TIMESTAMP" (verified by unit test).
  - id: AC8
    text: >
      A DiffTest with timeout shorter than binary runtime fails with a timeout message
      (verified by unit test using sleep or a slow command).
  - id: AC9
    text: >
      Production code (difftest.go + normalize.go) is between 200 and 350 lines.
